text:
sara: Heads up — invoice-preview showed a 12% token spike right after we flipped the new route-priority heuristic at 02:00 UTC. Not all tenants, mostly mid-size ones.
aj: can you paste the preview diff? is it tokens or req_count?
sara: looks like tokens. Preview delta shows +
```
{"tenant_id":"acme","route_id":"r-priority-v2","fallback_route":"r-std","tokens":120450,"prev_tokens":107200}
```
aj: hmm fallback_route present. Could be counting both primary+fallback when routing fails over?
mike: that was our fear. The routing proxy emits two meter events on fallback: one for attempted route (recorded) and one for fallback success. metric-ingest dedupe only keyed on request_id, but proxy sometimes rewrites request_id for routed retries.
sara: exact. I dug into a sample event pair — same session but different req_id suffix. metering-bot: detected 347 potential duplicate invoice events in the last hour for route-priority experiments (score>0.8).
anna: are we sure this is a metering ingest bug vs proxy behavior? which side should dedupe live on?
aj: debate: dedupe at ingest gives centralized control but loses semantics (we'd have to choose which event wins). dedupe at proxy risks missing legit dupes across retries.
mike: short-term fix: add canonical_request_id header in proxy that we propagate unchanged on internal retries. then ingest dedupe can use canonical_request_id+tenant to collapse. low-risk.
sara: agreed. Do we have an SDR for the proxy? ops-oncall: I can patch the proxy canary tomorrow morning (small traffic). Add header name `x-canonical-req-id`.
anna: what about historical previews? invoices already generated for yesterday — do we need a backfill to collapse dupes in the invoice ledger?
aj: yes. For any tenant where preview delta > 5% and route-priority enabled, run a backfill reconcile job that groups by canonical id where available, otherwise by a fingerprint heuristic. Risk: ledger is append-only; we'll emit corrective invoice adjustments.
mike: I'll add a lightweight fingerprint: sha1(req_path + client_ip + user_agent + session_id) and tag events until canonical header lands. We'll only collapse events that match within 5s window.
sara: timeline? we need console UX to reflect expected adjustments so finance isn't spooked.
aj: plan: (1) proxy canary tomorrow with header (2) ingest accept new header and use as dedupe key within 48h (3) run backfill for affected tenants in 72h, produce adjustment lines and post to invoice-preview feed with `adjustment:duplicate_collapse` flag.
anna: will console show both original preview and adjusted preview? Product: probably show adjusted and an audit trail.
sara: logged a ticket in billing (TICKET-4982). tagging finance + CS.
anna: small thought — can we detect double-counting purely via route_tag collisions? many edge cases though.
mike: route_tag can't distinguish retries that rewrite req_id. canonical header solves it. Also will emit a telemetry gauge for "duplicate_deduped_count" for SLOs.
aj: add console card: per-tenant "duplicate_dedupe_rate" and allow filter by route alias. That'll help product decide whether to pause rollout.
ops-oncall: I'll schedule the canary 03:30 PST and watch metrics; alert if preview-delta > 3% post-canary.
sara: thanks everyone. I'll ping finance once we have the adjustment preview. :thumbsup:
metering-bot: note — created anomaly ticket AM-176654 for the 12% spike; linked to TICKET-4982.
